title: Magnetic properties and structure of tetranuclear lanthanide complexes based on 8-hydroxylquinoline Schiff base derivative and β-diketone coligand

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.compound_name: Tetranuclear gadolinium dbm/L hydroxide complex, acetonitrile solvate

material_class.structural_family: Coplanar butterfly-like tetranuclear lanthanide complex with μ3-hydroxide bridges

synthesis.procedure: Under air, Gd(dbm)3·2H2O (0.02 mmol) and HL (0.02 mmol) were dissolved in acetonitrile (15 mL), acetone (5 mL), and ethanol (5 mL). The yellow solution was stirred for about 4 h at room temperature, filtered, and the filtrate was allowed to evaporate slowly under ambient conditions. Orange rhombic crystals formed after a few days.
synthesis.time: about 4 h stirring; a few days for crystallization
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution reaction followed by slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtered; filtrate slowly evaporated under ambient conditions to give orange rhombic crystals.

properties.summary: Weak intramolecular antiferromagnetic exchange is indicated by decreasing χMT on cooling. The complex exhibits a magnetocaloric effect.

source_locations.location: Results and Discussion, Descriptions of the complexes; Conclusion

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: One of five isomorphous tetranuclear complexes with four coplanar lanthanide ions in a butterfly-like, parallelogram framework. The detailed Dy analogue 3 establishes the shared μ3-hydroxide-bridged motif and approximately square-antiprismatic metal coordination.

properties.summary: The χMT product initially rises on cooling, consistent with possible weak ferromagnetic coupling, then falls at low temperature. Frequency-dependent ac susceptibility in zero dc field demonstrates slow magnetic relaxation characteristic of single-molecule magnet behavior.

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The four coplanar Dy(III) ions occupy the corners of a parallelogram with a butterfly topology and crystallographic inversion symmetry. Two μ3-hydroxide oxygen atoms each bridge a central ion to wingtip ions. Six L⁻ and four dbm⁻ ligands complete the molecular framework; the eight-coordinate Dy sites have distorted square-antiprismatic geometries. The shortest intramolecular Dy···Dy separation is 3.5621(3) Å.
